threats.threat_description: An attacker captures and replays or forges RF response messages to the vehicle RF transceiver, impersonating the legitimate key fob to gain unauthorized access or start the engine.

cybersecurity_goal.csg_statement: The Key Fob shall enforce the Authenticity, Confidentiality, and Integrity of RF Challenge-Response Messages against Manipulate Communications to prevent unauthorized vehicle unlocking and starting.

threats.threat_description: Sensitive cryptographic key material stored in the key fob could be extracted via side-channel attacks or physical tampering, compromising vehicle security.

cybersecurity_goal.csg_statement: The Key Fob shall protect the Confidentiality and Authenticity of Cryptographic Key Material against ATM-T0028: Hardware Fault Injection to prevent unauthorized vehicle unlocking and starting.

threats.threat_description: An attacker jams or floods the RF channel preventing the key fob from receiving challenges or sending responses, blocking legitimate vehicle access or start.
Physical tampering or modification of the LF antenna could cause false proximity signals, triggering unauthorized wake events or denial of service by disabling proximity detection.

cybersecurity_goal.csg_statement: The LF Antenna (Door Handle) shall enforce the Authenticity, Integrity, and Availability of the LF Proximity Signal against Physical Modification to prevent unauthorized vehicle wake/unlock or denial of entry/start for legitimate users.

threats.threat_description: An attacker physically disables or obstructs the LF antenna to prevent detection of the key fob, denying entry or start functionality.

cybersecurity_goal.csg_statement: The LF Antenna (Door Handle) shall enforce the Availability of the LF Proximity Signal against ATM-T0016: Physical Modification to prevent denial of legitimate vehicle entry and start functionality.
cybersecurity_goal.verification_method: Physical Tamper Testing / Functional Availability Test

threats.threat_description: An attacker uses a malicious external RF antenna to relay, amplify or spoof RF challenge or response signals, bypassing proximity or cryptographic protections.
linked_assets: RF Transceiver -> Vehicle Antenna RF Link

cybersecurity_goal.csg_statement: The Vehicle RF Antenna shall enforce the Authenticity, Confidentiality, and Integrity of RF Challenge-Response Messages on the Vehicle Antenna RF Link against ATM-T0007: Relay Communications to prevent unauthorized vehicle unlocking or starting.

threats.threat_description: Physical damage or jamming of the vehicle RF antenna prevents legitimate RF communications, denying key fob authentication and vehicle access/start.
linked_assets: RF Transceiver -> Vehicle Antenna RF Link

cybersecurity_goal.csg_statement: The Vehicle RF Antenna shall ensure the Availability and Authenticity of the RF Transceiver to Vehicle Antenna RF Link against Jamming or Denial of Service to prevent legitimate user lockout and vehicle immobilization.

threats.threat_description: Compromise of the RF transceiver firmware could allow an attacker to modify or forge forwarded authentication data, undermining the integrity of key fob responses before they reach the BCM.
threats.atm_technique_name: Modify OS Kernel, Boot Partition, or System Partition

cybersecurity_goal.csg_statement: The RF Transceiver (Vehicle) shall enforce the Authenticity and Integrity of Auth Data and RF Transceiver Firmware against ATM-T0022: Modify OS Kernel, Boot Partition, or System Partition to prevent unauthorized vehicle access or starting by forged authentication responses.

threats.threat_description: Malicious firmware or physical compromise of the RF transceiver could leak authentication data or keys to external attackers via the RF interface or internal channels.

cybersecurity_goal.csg_statement: The RF Transceiver (Vehicle) shall protect the Confidentiality and Authenticity of Auth Data and RF Transceiver Firmware against ATM-T0065: Short Range Wireless Communication to prevent unauthorized access to cryptographic keys and bypass of vehicle authentication mechanisms.

threats.threat_description: An attacker jams or blocks RF transceiver reception or transmission, preventing challenge-response exchanges and causing denial of vehicle access or start.

cybersecurity_goal.csg_statement: The RF Transceiver (Vehicle) shall enforce the Availability of RF Challenge-Response Messages against ATM-T0002: Jamming or Denial of Service to prevent authorized users from being denied vehicle access or start.

threats.threat_description: An attacker sends unauthorized commands to the RF transceiver control interface (BCM -> RF Transceiver Control Interface) to inject fake challenges or modify transmission parameters, potentially triggering unauthorized vehicle responses.

cybersecurity_goal.csg_statement: The RF Transceiver (Vehicle) shall enforce the Authenticity, Integrity, and Availability of the BCM -> RF Transceiver Control Interface against ATM-T0071: Unintended Vehicle Network Message to prevent unauthorized vehicle unlocking, starting, or activation of vehicle functions.

threats.threat_description: An attacker with physical access to the vehicle could connect to the debug or JTAG interface of the RF Transceiver hardware. By leveraging this interface, the attacker extracts sensitive authentication data and cryptographic keys stored or processed within the RF Transceiver Firmware. This direct hardware interface bypasses software protections, enabling covert exfiltration of Auth Data (RF response forwarded) to an external device, compromising vehicle authentication mechanisms.

cybersecurity_goal.csg_statement: The RF Transceiver (Vehicle) shall protect the Confidentiality and Authenticity of Auth Data (RF response forwarded) and RF Transceiver Firmware against ATM-T0073: Physical Access to prevent unauthorized vehicle entry or starting.

threats.threat_description: An attacker impersonates the BCM on the CAN bus to send unauthorized lock/unlock or start authorization commands to Door ECU or Start Authorization ECU, bypassing authentication.

cybersecurity_goal.csg_statement: The Body Control Module (BCM) shall enforce the Authenticity and Integrity of CAN Lock/Unlock Message and Powertrain Start Interface against ATM-T0071: Unintended Vehicle Network Message to prevent unauthorized vehicle entry and engine start.

threats.threat_description: Modification or compromise of BCM firmware or configuration data could cause unauthorized issuance of lock/unlock or start commands, or bypass cryptographic verification.
threats.atm_technique_name: Modify OS Kernel, Boot Partition, or System Partition

cybersecurity_goal.csg_statement: The Body Control Module (BCM) shall enforce the Integrity, Authenticity, Confidentiality, and Availability of Firmware and Configuration Data against Modify OS Kernel, Boot Partition, or System Partition to prevent unauthorized issuance of lock/unlock or engine start commands and bypass of cryptographic verification.

threats.threat_description: Insufficient logging or lack of secure audit data in BCM firmware could allow an attacker or insider to deny having issued unauthorized lock/unlock or start commands.

cybersecurity_goal.csg_statement: The Body Control Module (BCM) shall enforce the Integrity, Authenticity, and Accountability of Firmware Audit Logs against ATM-T0071: Unintended Vehicle Network Message to prevent denial of unauthorized lock/unlock or engine start command issuance and ensure traceability for forensic investigations.

threats.threat_description: Exposure of BCM configuration, cryptographic keys, or cryptographic verification results through insecure storage or debug interfaces could leak sensitive data to attackers.

cybersecurity_goal.csg_statement: The Body Control Module (BCM) shall protect the Confidentiality, Integrity, and Authenticity of Firmware in BCM and BCM Configuration and Access Policies against ATM-T0040: Unsecured Credentials to prevent unauthorized access, key cloning, or bypassing of immobilizer functions.

threats.threat_description: An attacker floods the BCM with fake LF wake/proximity events or malformed RF responses causing resource exhaustion, preventing legitimate authentication flows.

cybersecurity_goal.csg_statement: The Body Control Module (BCM) shall enforce the Availability and Integrity of LF Proximity Signal and Auth Data (RF response forwarded) against ATM-T0002: Jamming or Denial of Service to prevent legitimate users from being unable to unlock or start the vehicle.

threats.threat_description: An attacker exploits vulnerabilities in the BCM firmware or access control policies to gain unauthorized privileges, enabling manipulation of cryptographic verification or token issuance.

cybersecurity_goal.csg_statement: The Body Control Module (BCM) shall enforce the Authenticity, Integrity, Confidentiality, and Availability of Firmware and Access Control Policies against Exploit OS Vulnerability to prevent unauthorized privilege escalation and manipulation of secure vehicle functions.

threats.threat_description: An attacker uses analog sensor manipulation techniques to interfere with the Body Control Module's sensor inputs, such as ultrasonic parking sensors or door lock status sensors. By jamming or spoofing these analog signals, the attacker causes the BCM firmware to misinterpret vehicle state changes, such as falsely detecting door unlock events or engine start commands. Because the BCM firmware lacks secure logging and robust audit trails for these sensor inputs, the attacker or insider can later deny having triggered these unauthorized actions, complicating incident investigation and accountability.

cybersecurity_goal.csg_statement: The Body Control Module (BCM) shall enforce the Authenticity, Integrity, and Accountability of Firmware in BCM against ATM-T0004: Analog Sensor Attacks to prevent unauthorized vehicle state changes and hindered incident investigation.
cybersecurity_goal.verification_method: Penetration Test / Log Audit / Interface Analysis

threats.threat_description: An attacker sends forged unlock/lock commands on the CAN bus to the Door ECU to unlock doors without proper authentication.

cybersecurity_goal.csg_statement: The Door ECU shall enforce the Authenticity and Integrity of CAN Lock/Unlock Message and Door Lock/Unlock Command against ATM-T0071: Unintended Vehicle Network Message to prevent unauthorized unlocking of vehicle doors.

threats.threat_description: Modification of Door ECU firmware or configuration could allow bypassing token verification or unauthorized control of the door lock actuator.
threats.atm_technique_name: Modify OS Kernel, Boot Partition, or System Partition

cybersecurity_goal.csg_statement: The Door ECU shall enforce the Authenticity, Integrity, and Availability of Door Lock/Unlock Command against ATM-T0022: Modify OS Kernel, Boot Partition, or System Partition to prevent unauthorized control of the door lock actuator and unauthorized vehicle entry.

threats.threat_description: Compromise of Door ECU could leak authorization tokens or unlock command details, aiding attackers in crafting unauthorized messages.

cybersecurity_goal.csg_statement: The Door ECU shall protect the Confidentiality and Authenticity of the Start Authorization Token against ATM-T0040: Unsecured Credentials to prevent unauthorized vehicle entry or starting.

threats.threat_description: An attacker jams or floods the CAN bus with spurious lock/unlock messages preventing legitimate door control commands from being processed.

cybersecurity_goal.csg_statement: The Door ECU shall enforce the Availability and Authenticity of CAN Lock/Unlock Messages against ATM-T0068: CAN Bus Denial of Service to prevent temporary loss of door locking and unlocking functionality.

threats.threat_description: Exploiting vulnerabilities in the Door ECU to bypass token verification or escalate privileges to control door actuators directly.

cybersecurity_goal.csg_statement: The Door ECU shall enforce the Authenticity, Integrity, and Availability of Door Lock/Unlock Command against ATM-T0026: Exploit OS Vulnerability to prevent unauthorized unlocking or locking of vehicle doors.

threats.threat_description: An attacker with physical or network access to the vehicle's diagnostic interface exploits standard diagnostic protocols to send unauthorized commands to the Door ECU. By leveraging diagnostic services intended for legitimate maintenance, the attacker issues commands that directly actuate the door lock/unlock mechanism without proper authentication, potentially enabling unauthorized entry or preventing legitimate access.
threats.atm_technique_name: Abuse Standard Diagnostic Protocol for Affecting Vehicle Function

cybersecurity_goal.csg_statement: The Door ECU shall enforce the Authenticity, Integrity, and Availability of Door Lock/Unlock Command against ATM-T0067: Abuse Standard Diagnostic Protocol for Affecting Vehicle Function to prevent unauthorized entry or entrapment of occupants.

threats.threat_description: An attacker with initial access to a lower-privileged ECU abuses the standard diagnostic protocol’s ‘write memory by address’ service on the Door ECU to upload and execute malicious code. This code grants the attacker persistent control over the door locking mechanism, allowing unauthorized unlocking or lockout of the vehicle doors without triggering standard authentication checks.
threats.atm_technique_name: Abuse Standard Diagnostic Protocol for Lateral Movement

cybersecurity_goal.csg_statement: The Door ECU shall enforce the Authenticity, Integrity, and Availability of Door Lock/Unlock Command against ATM-T0050: Abuse Standard Diagnostic Protocol for Lateral Movement to prevent unauthorized and persistent control of vehicle doors.
cybersecurity_goal.verification_method: Penetration Test / Diagnostic Service Access Control Validation

threats.threat_description: An attacker forges start authorization commands or tokens on the CAN bus to enable engine start without proper authentication.

cybersecurity_goal.csg_statement: The Start Authorization ECU shall enforce the Authenticity and Integrity of Engine Start Command on the Powertrain Start Interface against ATM-T0071: Unintended Vehicle Network Message to prevent unauthorized engine start and vehicle theft.

threats.threat_description: Compromise of the Start Authorization ECU firmware or configuration could allow bypassing token verification and unauthorized enabling of engine start.
threats.atm_technique_name: Modify OS Kernel, Boot Partition, or System Partition

cybersecurity_goal.csg_statement: The Start Authorization ECU shall enforce the Integrity and Authenticity of the Engine Start Command against ATM-T0022: Modify OS Kernel, Boot Partition, or System Partition to prevent unauthorized engine start and vehicle theft.

threats.threat_description: Leakage of start authorization tokens or authorization context from the Start Authorization ECU could aid attackers in replay or forging attacks.

cybersecurity_goal.csg_statement: The Start Authorization ECU shall protect the Confidentiality and Authenticity of the Start Authorization Token against Network Sniffing to prevent unauthorized vehicle starting and immobilizer bypass.

threats.threat_description: Jamming or flooding of the CAN bus or Start Authorization ECU interface to Engine ECU prevents engine start even with valid tokens.

cybersecurity_goal.csg_statement: The Start Authorization ECU shall enforce the Availability, Integrity, and Authenticity of the Powertrain Start Interface against ATM-T0068: CAN Bus Denial of Service to prevent unauthorized denial of engine start with valid authentication tokens.

threats.threat_description: Exploitation of vulnerabilities in the Start Authorization ECU to bypass token checks and directly command engine start.

cybersecurity_goal.csg_statement: The Start Authorization ECU shall enforce the Authenticity, Integrity, and Availability of the Engine Start Command against Exploit OS Vulnerability to prevent unauthorized engine start and vehicle theft.

threats.threat_description: An attacker with local access to the Start Authorization ECU exploits command-line interfaces or scripting capabilities to search and extract sensitive start authorization tokens stored in local files, logs, or volatile memory. This unauthorized retrieval of tokens enables the attacker to analyze or replay authorization sequences, potentially bypassing start authorization controls.

cybersecurity_goal.csg_statement: The Start Authorization ECU shall protect the Confidentiality and Authenticity of the Start Authorization Token against ATM-T0059: Data from Local System to prevent unauthorized vehicle starting.
cybersecurity_goal.verification_method: Penetration Testing / Memory and File System Analysis

threats.threat_description: Since the CAN bus is a broadcast medium, attackers with physical access could eavesdrop on lock/unlock and start authorization messages, potentially revealing authorization tokens or sensitive command data.

cybersecurity_goal.csg_statement: The CAN Bus shall protect the Confidentiality and Authenticity of lock/unlock and start authorization messages against ATM-T0038: Network Sniffing to prevent unauthorized vehicle access and operation.

threats.threat_description: An attacker floods the CAN bus with spurious messages causing message collisions or delays, disrupting legitimate lock/unlock or start commands.

cybersecurity_goal.csg_statement: The CAN Bus shall enforce the Availability and Integrity of In-Vehicle CAN (broadcast medium) against ATM-T0068: CAN Bus Denial of Service to prevent disruption of legitimate lock/unlock and engine start commands.

threats.threat_description: Compromise of HSM firmware or unauthorized modification could lead to extraction or misuse of cryptographic keys, or issuance of unauthorized authorization tokens.

cybersecurity_goal.csg_statement: The HSM / Secure Enclave shall enforce the Confidentiality, Integrity, Authenticity, and Availability of HSM Firmware / Secure Boot Measurements and Cryptographic Key Material against ATM-T0075: Compromise Cryptographic Security to prevent unauthorized extraction or misuse of keys, issuance of unauthorized tokens, and persistent vehicle compromise.

threats.threat_description: An attacker impersonates the HSM or forges HSM API responses to the BCM, providing false verification results or authorization tokens.

cybersecurity_goal.csg_statement: The HSM / Secure Enclave shall enforce the Authenticity, Integrity, and Confidentiality of the Restricted HSM API and Start Authorization Token against ATM-T0003: Manipulate Communications to prevent unauthorized vehicle start and bypass of cryptographic checks.
cybersecurity_goal.verification_method: Penetration Test / Interface Fuzzing / Protocol Analysis

threats.threat_description: Lack of secure logging or attestation data could allow the HSM or its operator to deny having issued certain tokens or verification results.
threats.atm_technique_name: Modify OS Kernel, Boot Partition, or System Partition

cybersecurity_goal.csg_statement: The HSM / Secure Enclave shall enforce the Authenticity, Integrity, and Non-repudiation of HSM Attestation / Measurement Data against ATM-T0022: Modify OS Kernel, Boot Partition, or System Partition to prevent denial of token issuance or verification traceability.

threats.threat_description: Leakage of cryptographic keys, firmware, or attestation data from the HSM could compromise overall vehicle security.

cybersecurity_goal.csg_statement: The HSM / Secure Enclave shall protect the Confidentiality, Integrity, and Authenticity of Cryptographic Key Material and HSM Firmware / Secure Boot Measurements against ATM-T0006: Removable Media to prevent compromise of cryptographic secrets, unauthorized firmware updates, and bypassing of secure boot.

threats.threat_description: An attacker prevents the HSM from processing verification requests or generating tokens by flooding the API or exploiting firmware bugs, denying authentication services.

cybersecurity_goal.csg_statement: The HSM / Secure Enclave shall enforce the Availability, Integrity, and Authenticity of the Restricted HSM API against ATM-T0002: Jamming or Denial of Service to prevent loss of authentication services and disabling of critical vehicle functions.
cybersecurity_goal.verification_method: Penetration Testing / Fault Injection / Interface Load Testing

threats.threat_description: Exploitation of vulnerabilities inside the HSM or its API to extract keys or issue tokens beyond authorized limits.

cybersecurity_goal.csg_statement: The HSM / Secure Enclave shall enforce the Confidentiality, Integrity, Authenticity, and Availability of Cryptographic Key Material and Restricted HSM API against ATM-T0027: Exploit Isolated Execution Environment Vulnerability to prevent unauthorized extraction of keys, issuance of tokens, and subsequent vehicle compromise.
cybersecurity_goal.verification_method: Penetration Testing / Interface Fuzzing / Code Review

threats.threat_description: An attacker injects malware into the vehicle's firmware update process that employs a known encryption algorithm to covertly exfiltrate cryptographic key material from the HSM. Since the encryption keys are hardcoded within the malware, reverse engineering the malware sample allows the adversary to recover these keys, thereby compromising the confidentiality of the HSM's cryptographic assets.

cybersecurity_goal.csg_statement: The HSM / Secure Enclave shall protect the Confidentiality, Authenticity, and Integrity of Cryptographic Key Material and HSM Firmware / Secure Boot Measurements against ATM-T0066: Standard Cryptographic Protocol to prevent unauthorized disclosure and misuse of cryptographic secrets leading to severe compromise of vehicle security functions.
cybersecurity_goal.verification_method: Penetration Test / Firmware Analysis / Interface Fuzzing

threats.threat_description: Compromise of the crypto engine internals could allow generating forged authorization tokens or bypassing verification checks.

cybersecurity_goal.csg_statement: The Crypto Engine shall enforce the Confidentiality, Integrity, Authenticity, and Availability of Cryptographic Key Material against ATM-T0075: Compromise Cryptographic Security to prevent unauthorized vehicle access, immobilizer bypass, and manipulation of secure communications.
cybersecurity_goal.verification_method: Penetration Testing / Security Audit / Interface Analysis

threats.threat_description: Leakage of cryptographic keys or verification results from the crypto engine could aid attackers in forging tokens or responses.

cybersecurity_goal.csg_statement: The Crypto Engine shall protect the Confidentiality, Authenticity, and Integrity of Cryptographic Key Material against ATM-T0038: Network Sniffing to prevent unauthorized access to protected vehicle functions or backend services.

threats.threat_description: Modification or unauthorized access to the cryptographic key store could allow key replacement or extraction, undermining all cryptographic protections.

cybersecurity_goal.csg_statement: The Cryptographic Key Store shall protect the Confidentiality, Integrity, Authenticity, and Availability of Cryptographic Key Material against ATM-T0023: Modify Isolated Execution Environment to prevent compromise of secure boot, secure communication, and authentication mechanisms.
cybersecurity_goal.verification_method: Penetration Test / Secure Enclave Interface Analysis

threats.threat_description: Extraction of cryptographic keys from the key store, for example via side-channel or fault injection attacks, would compromise vehicle authentication.

cybersecurity_goal.csg_statement: The Cryptographic Key Store shall protect the Confidentiality and Authenticity of Cryptographic Key Material against ATM-T0028: Hardware Fault Injection to prevent unauthorized vehicle authentication and credential cloning.
cybersecurity_goal.verification_method: Penetration Testing / Side-Channel and Fault Injection Analysis

threats.threat_description: An attacker exploits a vulnerability in the cryptographic key store firmware update process to bypass existing code integrity checks, enabling them to install unauthorized firmware. This malicious firmware then manipulates the cryptographic key material to extract or replace keys without detection.

cybersecurity_goal.csg_statement: The Cryptographic Key Store shall enforce the Confidentiality, Integrity, and Authenticity of Cryptographic Key Material against Bypass Code Integrity Protections to prevent unauthorized extraction or replacement of keys leading to vehicle compromise.
cybersecurity_goal.verification_method: Penetration Test / Firmware Update Process Review

threats.threat_description: Physical tampering with the door lock actuator could allow manual unlocking or jamming the actuator to prevent locking.

cybersecurity_goal.csg_statement: The Door Lock Actuator shall enforce the Authenticity, Integrity, and Availability of Door Lock/Unlock Command against ATM-T0016: Physical Modification to prevent unauthorized entry or inability to secure the vehicle.

threats.threat_description: An attacker physically disables or jams the door lock actuator to prevent locking or unlocking, denying vehicle access control.

cybersecurity_goal.csg_statement: The Door Lock Actuator shall enforce the Availability of Door Lock/Unlock Command against ATM-T0002: Jamming or Denial of Service to prevent denial of legitimate vehicle access or securing.
cybersecurity_goal.verification_method: Physical Tampering Test / Functional Availability Test

threats.threat_description: An attacker who gains local access to the body controller ECU associated with the Door Lock Actuator exploits a vulnerability to execute arbitrary code. This unauthorized control allows the attacker to send forged Door Lock/Unlock Commands, resulting in unauthorized unlocking of the vehicle doors without physical manipulation of the actuator.

cybersecurity_goal.csg_statement: The Door Lock Actuator shall enforce the Authenticity, Integrity, and Availability of Door Lock/Unlock Command against ATM-T0069: Local Function to prevent unauthorized unlocking of vehicle doors.

threats.threat_description: Compromise of the Engine ECU or inverter firmware could allow bypassing start authorization, enabling engine start without valid tokens.
threats.atm_technique_name: Modify OS Kernel, Boot Partition, or System Partition

cybersecurity_goal.csg_statement: The Engine ECU / Inverter shall enforce the Integrity and Authenticity of the Engine Start Command against ATM-T0022: Modify OS Kernel, Boot Partition, or System Partition to prevent unauthorized engine start and vehicle theft.

threats.threat_description: An attacker blocks or jams the powertrain interface messages from the Start Authorization ECU, preventing engine start despite valid authorization.

cybersecurity_goal.csg_statement: The Engine ECU / Inverter shall ensure the Availability of the Powertrain Start Interface against ATM-T0002: Jamming or Denial of Service to prevent unauthorized immobilization of the vehicle despite valid start authorization.
cybersecurity_goal.functional_boundary: In-Vehicle / Wired and Wireless Communication Channel

threats.threat_description: An attacker generates fake LF wake/proximity signals causing the LF receiver to produce false wake events to the BCM, resulting in unauthorized challenge emission and potential denial of service.
linked_assets: LF Receiver -> BCM Event / Control Link

cybersecurity_goal.csg_statement: The LF Receiver / LF Front-End shall enforce the Authenticity and Availability of the LF Proximity Signal and LF Receiver to BCM Event / Control Link against ATM-T0003: Manipulate Communications to prevent unauthorized challenge emission and denial of service.

threats.threat_description: Blocking or jamming the LF frequency prevents the LF receiver from detecting legitimate key fob proximity, denying vehicle wake and subsequent authentication.

cybersecurity_goal.csg_statement: The LF Receiver / LF Front-End shall ensure the Availability of the LF Proximity Signal against ATM-T0002: Jamming or Denial of Service to prevent legitimate user lockout and vehicle inaccessibility.

threats.threat_description: Physical modification of the LF receiver hardware or firmware could cause omission or false reporting of wake events to the BCM.
linked_assets: LF Receiver -> BCM Event / Control Link

cybersecurity_goal.csg_statement: The LF Receiver / LF Front-End shall enforce the Integrity, Availability, and Authenticity of the LF Receiver to BCM Event / Control Link against Physical Modification to prevent denial of legitimate keyless entry/start or unauthorized triggering of BCM actions.
cybersecurity_goal.verification_method: Test / Hardware Inspection / Firmware Integrity Verification

threats.threat_description: Relay attacks that extend the effective range of the key fob by relaying LF and RF signals between the vehicle and remote key fob, bypassing proximity protections. This spans ANT_RF_1, RF_1, ANT_1, LF_RX_1, and communication assets C1, C2, C10.
linked_assets: RF Transceiver -> Vehicle Antenna RF Link

cybersecurity_goal.csg_statement: The Vehicle Access Control System shall enforce the Authenticity and Integrity of LF Proximity Signals and RF Challenge-Response Messages against ATM-T0007: Relay Communications to prevent unauthorized vehicle unlocking and starting.

threats.threat_description: Firmware compromise or unauthorized modification in any ECU, especially BCM, RF transceiver, or HSM, allowing attackers to forge or manipulate authentication data, tokens, or commands across multiple data flows such as DF6 (RF_1->BCM_1), DF7/DF8 (BCM<->HSM), and CAN messages (DF4, DF5).
threats.atm_technique_name: Modify OS Kernel, Boot Partition, or System Partition

cybersecurity_goal.csg_statement: The Body Control Module, RF Transceiver, and Hardware Security Module shall enforce the Authenticity, Integrity, Confidentiality, and Availability of ECU Firmware and Secure Boot Measurements against Modify OS Kernel, Boot Partition, or System Partition to prevent persistent unauthorized control over authentication and authorization processes leading to vehicle unlocking, starting, or disabling of security features.
cybersecurity_goal.verification_method: Penetration Test / Secure Boot Verification / Firmware Integrity Check

threats.threat_description: Lack of secure, tamper-proof logging of authentication and command events across BCM, HSM, and ECUs could allow attackers or insiders to deny unauthorized actions. This affects components BCM_1, HSM_1, ECU_DOOR, ECU_START and assets I3, I10.
threats.atm_technique_name: Denial of Service on Vehicle Function

cybersecurity_goal.csg_statement: The BCM, HSM, ECU_DOOR, and ECU_START shall enforce the Integrity, Authenticity, and Accountability of Authentication and Command Event Logs against ATM-T0072: Denial of Service on Vehicle Function to prevent repudiation of unauthorized actions and loss of forensic evidence.

threats.threat_description: Broadcast nature of CAN bus and wireless communications allows attackers with physical or RF proximity to eavesdrop on challenge-response messages (C2), authorization tokens (I4), or commands (C3, C5), aiding replay or forgery attacks.

cybersecurity_goal.csg_statement: The Vehicle Communication Interfaces shall protect the Confidentiality and Authenticity of RF Challenge-Response Messages, CAN Lock/Unlock Message, Powertrain Start Interface, and Start Authorization Token against ATM-T0038: Network Sniffing to prevent unauthorized vehicle unlocking or starting.

threats.threat_description: Jamming or flooding attacks on LF and RF wireless channels, or on the CAN bus, can disrupt keyless entry and start functionality by preventing legitimate communication or overwhelming ECUs like BCM, RF transceiver, or Start Authorization ECU.

cybersecurity_goal.csg_statement: The Body Control Module (BCM) shall enforce the Availability of LF Proximity Signal, RF Challenge-Response Messages, and In-Vehicle CAN communications against ATM-T0002: Jamming or Denial of Service to prevent loss of keyless entry and start functionality.

threats.threat_description: Vulnerabilities in ECU or HSM firmware could allow attackers to escalate privileges, bypass authentication or token verification, and issue unauthorized commands across the system, affecting BCM, HSM, ECU_DOOR, and ECU_START.

cybersecurity_goal.csg_statement: The BCM and HSM shall enforce the Authenticity, Integrity, and Availability of Firmware, Secure Boot Measurements, and Critical Command Interfaces against ATM-T0024: Abuse Elevation Control Mechanism to prevent unauthorized vehicle entry, unauthorized engine start, and compromise of system trustworthiness.
cybersecurity_goal.verification_method: Penetration Test / Firmware Analysis / Interface Authentication Test

threats.threat_description: An attacker intercepts and replays or manipulates the Challenge-Response Nonces (I2) exchanged between the key fob and vehicle, enabling replay or relay attacks to gain unauthorized access or start the engine.

cybersecurity_goal.csg_statement: The Key Fob and Vehicle Authentication Module shall enforce the Authenticity and Confidentiality of Challenge-Response Nonces against ATM-T0007: Relay Communications to prevent unauthorized unlocking and starting of the vehicle.

threats.threat_description: An attacker intercepts and analyzes Message Annotations (I6) including security and freshness tags in communication protocols, potentially leaking protocol state or facilitating targeted attacks on the PKES system.

Manipulation or injection of Message Annotations (I6) within the communication flows could cause the BCM or other components to misinterpret message freshness, authorization, or identifiers, leading to unauthorized unlock or engine start.

cybersecurity_goal.csg_statement: The Body Control Module (BCM) shall enforce the Authenticity, Integrity, and Availability of Message Annotations exchanged with ECU_DOOR and ECU_START against Modify Bus Message to prevent unauthorized vehicle unlocking or engine start.

threats.threat_description: Exposure or leakage of RF receive metadata (C11) such as RSSI or timestamps could be exploited by attackers to perform relay, spoofing, or location tracking attacks against the PKES system.

cybersecurity_goal.csg_statement: The PKES system shall protect the Confidentiality, Authenticity, and Privacy of RF receive metadata (RSSI/timestamp) against ATM-T0043: Location Tracking to prevent unauthorized vehicle access, theft, or privacy violation through tracking.

threats.threat_description: An attacker manipulates RF receive metadata (C11) reported by the RF transceiver to the BCM, causing incorrect proximity or freshness decisions and potentially enabling relay or replay attacks.

cybersecurity_goal.csg_statement: The Body Control Module (BCM) shall enforce the Authenticity, Integrity, and Availability of RF receive metadata (RSSI/timestamp) on the RF_1 to BCM_1 interface against Modify Bus Message to prevent unauthorized vehicle unlocking or starting due to incorrect proximity or freshness decisions.

threats.threat_description: An attacker spoofs or forges the LF proximity trigger signal (DF1) from the LF antenna to the key fob, causing false wake-up events and unauthorized challenge-response sequences.

cybersecurity_goal.csg_statement: The LF Communication Module shall enforce the Authenticity, Integrity, and Availability of LF Proximity Trigger Signals between the LF Antenna and Key Fob against Manipulate Communications to prevent unauthorized challenge-response events and potential vehicle theft.

threats.threat_description: Blocking or jamming the LF proximity trigger signal (DF1) prevents the key fob from detecting vehicle presence, denying legitimate entry or start attempts.

cybersecurity_goal.csg_statement: The External Antenna System shall enforce the Availability of the LF Proximity Trigger Signal against Jamming or Denial of Service to prevent denial of legitimate vehicle entry or start by authorized users.

threats.threat_description: Modification or manipulation of the RF challenge sent to the key fob (DF2) could cause incorrect authentication flows or denial of legitimate challenge processing.

cybersecurity_goal.csg_statement: The RF Communication Module shall enforce the Authenticity, Integrity, and Availability of RF Challenge Messages against ATM-T0070: Modify Bus Message to prevent denial of legitimate keyless entry and start requests.

threats.threat_description: Jamming or blocking the RF challenge flow (DF2) prevents the key fob from receiving authentication challenges, denying vehicle access or start.
An attacker forges or modifies the RF response message from the key fob (DF3) to the RF transceiver, bypassing authentication and gaining unauthorized access or engine start.
threats.atm_technique_name: Reprogram Co-Located Computing Device for Privilege Escalation

cybersecurity_goal.csg_statement: The RF Transceiver shall enforce the Authenticity, Confidentiality, and Integrity of RF Response Messages of EXT_1 and RF_1 against ATM-T0030: Reprogram Co-Located Computing Device for Privilege Escalation to prevent unauthorized vehicle unlocking and engine start.

threats.threat_description: Blocking or jamming the RF response message (DF3) prevents the vehicle from receiving valid authentication data, denying access or start.

cybersecurity_goal.csg_statement: The RF Communication Module shall enforce the Availability of RF Authentication Messages of EXT_1 and RF_1 against ATM-T0002: Jamming or Denial of Service to prevent denial of vehicle access or start for legitimate users.

threats.threat_description: An attacker injects forged lock/unlock CAN messages (DF4) from the BCM to the Door ECU to control door locking without proper authorization.

cybersecurity_goal.csg_statement: The Door ECU shall enforce the Authenticity and Integrity of lock/unlock CAN messages from the Body Control Module against ATM-T0071: Unintended Vehicle Network Message to prevent unauthorized locking or unlocking of vehicle doors.

threats.threat_description: An attacker blocks or floods the CAN message flow (DF4) to the Door ECU, preventing legitimate door lock/unlock commands from being processed.

cybersecurity_goal.csg_statement: The Door ECU shall enforce the Availability, Integrity, and Authenticity of lock/unlock command data flow between the Body Control Module and the Door ECU against CAN Bus Denial of Service to prevent loss of door locking and unlocking functionality.

threats.threat_description: An attacker forges start authorization CAN messages (DF5) from the BCM to the Start Authorization ECU, enabling engine start without proper authentication.

cybersecurity_goal.csg_statement: The Start Authorization ECU shall enforce the Authenticity and Integrity of start authorization messages from the Body Control Module against ATM-T0071: Unintended Vehicle Network Message to prevent unauthorized engine start and vehicle theft.

threats.threat_description: Blocking or jamming the start authorization CAN messages (DF5) prevents the engine from starting even with valid authorization tokens.

cybersecurity_goal.csg_statement: The Body Control Module and Engine Control Unit shall enforce the Availability and Authenticity of start authorization messages between BCM_1 and ECU_START against CAN Bus Denial of Service to prevent unauthorized immobilization of the vehicle.

threats.threat_description: Modification of Auth Data forwarded by the RF transceiver to the BCM (DF6) could cause incorrect authentication decisions or replay attacks.

cybersecurity_goal.csg_statement: The RF transceiver shall enforce the Authenticity, Integrity, and Availability of authentication data forwarded to the Body Control Module against Modify Bus Message to prevent unauthorized vehicle access, starting, or denial of service.

threats.threat_description: Blocking or delaying the Auth Data flow (DF6) from the RF transceiver to the BCM disrupts authentication processing and can deny vehicle access or start.
threats.atm_technique_name: Denial of Service on Vehicle Function

cybersecurity_goal.csg_statement: The RF transceiver and Body Control Module shall enforce the Availability and Authenticity of the authentication data flow between RF_1 and BCM_1 against ATM-T0072: Denial of Service on Vehicle Function to prevent legitimate users from being denied vehicle access or start.

threats.threat_description: An attacker forges or manipulates the restricted API call from BCM to HSM (DF7) to request unauthorized cryptographic verification or token generation.

cybersecurity_goal.csg_statement: The Body Control Module and Hardware Security Module shall enforce the Authenticity, Integrity, and Confidentiality of restricted API calls over data flow DF7 against Modify Bus Message to prevent unauthorized cryptographic operations and access to protected vehicle functions.
cybersecurity_goal.verification_method: Interface Fuzzing / Penetration Testing / Message Authentication Validation

threats.threat_description: Flooding or blocking the restricted API calls (DF7) between BCM and HSM denies cryptographic verification services, preventing authentication.

cybersecurity_goal.csg_statement: The Body Control Module shall ensure the Availability and Authenticity of cryptographic verification services between BCM and HSM against Jamming or Denial of Service to prevent unauthorized access or failure of authentication-dependent vehicle functions.

threats.threat_description: An attacker forges or tampers with the crypto result or authorization token returned from the HSM to the BCM (DF8) to grant unauthorized unlock or engine start.
threats.atm_technique_name: Reprogram Co-Located Computing Device for Privilege Escalation

cybersecurity_goal.csg_statement: The HSM-to-BCM Communication Interface shall enforce the Authenticity, Integrity, and Availability of Authorization Tokens against ATM-T0030: Reprogram Co-Located Computing Device for Privilege Escalation to prevent unauthorized vehicle unlocking or engine start.
cybersecurity_goal.verification_method: Penetration Test / Interface Fuzzing / Message Authentication Validation

threats.threat_description: Blocking or delaying the HSM response (DF8) to the BCM causes denial of authorization tokens, preventing door unlock or engine start.

cybersecurity_goal.csg_statement: The HSM-to-BCM Communication Interface shall enforce the Availability and Authenticity of Authorization Token Transmission against ATM-T0002: Jamming or Denial of Service to prevent denial of door unlocking or engine start.

threats.threat_description: Manipulation of the Door ECU to Door Lock Actuator signal (DF9) could cause unauthorized door unlocking or prevent locking.

cybersecurity_goal.csg_statement: The Door ECU shall enforce the Authenticity, Integrity, and Availability of the Door Lock Actuator control signals against Modify Bus Message to prevent unauthorized door unlocking or locking prevention.

threats.threat_description: Blocking or jamming the door actuator control signal (DF9) denies physical locking or unlocking of doors.

cybersecurity_goal.csg_statement: The ECU_DOOR shall enforce the Availability and Integrity of the door actuator control signal between ECU_DOOR and DOOR_ACT_1 against ATM-T0002: Jamming or Denial of Service to prevent unauthorized access or lockout due to failed door locking or unlocking.
cybersecurity_goal.functional_boundary: In-Vehicle / Wired or Wireless Signal Path

threats.threat_description: Manipulation or forgery of the powertrain start interface command (DF10) from Start Authorization ECU to Engine ECU could enable unauthorized engine start or prevent authorized start.

cybersecurity_goal.csg_statement: The Start Authorization ECU shall enforce the Authenticity, Integrity, and Availability of the powertrain start interface command to the Engine ECU against Modify Bus Message to prevent unauthorized engine start or denial of legitimate start.
cybersecurity_goal.functional_boundary: In-Vehicle Network (Start Authorization ECU <-> Engine ECU)
cybersecurity_goal.verification_method: Penetration Test / Interface Message Authentication Validation

threats.threat_description: Blocking or jamming the powertrain start interface messages (DF10) prevents engine start even with valid authorization.

cybersecurity_goal.csg_statement: The ECU_START and ENGINE_ECU shall enforce the Availability and Authenticity of start authorization messages against ATM-T0002: Jamming or Denial of Service to prevent unauthorized immobilization of the vehicle during legitimate start attempts.

threats.threat_description: An attacker forges or modifies the unlock command including authorization token from BCM to Door ECU (DF11), enabling unauthorized door unlock without proper authentication.

cybersecurity_goal.csg_statement: The Body Control Module and Door ECU shall enforce the Authenticity and Integrity of unlock command messages against Modify Bus Message to prevent unauthorized vehicle door unlocking.

threats.threat_description: Blocking or jamming the unlock command flow (DF11) prevents doors from unlocking even with valid authorization tokens.

cybersecurity_goal.csg_statement: The Body Control Module and Door ECU shall enforce the Availability of the Unlock Command Communication Channel against Jamming or Denial of Service to prevent authorized users from being unable to unlock the vehicle doors.

threats.threat_description: An attacker manipulates the internal HSM flow between Crypto Engine and Cryptographic Key Store (DF12) to intercept, extract, or replace cryptographic keys or metadata, compromising the entire cryptographic verification process.

cybersecurity_goal.csg_statement: The HSM Internal Data Path shall enforce the Confidentiality, Integrity, and Authenticity of cryptographic keys and metadata against ATM-T0075: Compromise Cryptographic Security to prevent unauthorized code execution, key exfiltration, or forging of cryptographic operations across the vehicle platform.
cybersecurity_goal.verification_method: Penetration Testing / Interface Monitoring / Hardware Security Evaluation

threats.threat_description: Disruption or blocking of the internal HSM communications on the secure bus (DF12) can prevent cryptographic operations, denying verification and token generation.

cybersecurity_goal.csg_statement: The Hardware Security Module (HSM) shall ensure the Availability, Integrity, and Authenticity of internal cryptographic communications between CRYPTO_ENG_1 and KEYSTORE_1 against ATM-T0002: Jamming or Denial of Service to prevent loss of cryptographic services affecting secure boot, secure diagnostics, or immobilizer functions.

threats.threat_description: An attacker forges or modifies the explicit token-bearing start authorization flow (DF13) from BCM to Start Authorization ECU, enabling unauthorized engine start.
threats.atm_technique_name: Reprogram Co-Located Computing Device for Privilege Escalation

cybersecurity_goal.csg_statement: The Body Control Module and Start Authorization ECU shall enforce the Authenticity and Integrity of start authorization messages between BCM_1 and ECU_START against ATM-T0030: Reprogram Co-Located Computing Device for Privilege Escalation to prevent unauthorized engine start and vehicle theft.

threats.threat_description: Blocking or jamming the token-bearing start authorization flow (DF13) prevents authorized engine start commands from reaching the Start Authorization ECU.

cybersecurity_goal.csg_statement: The BCM_1 and Start Authorization ECU shall ensure the Availability and Authenticity of the token-bearing start authorization flow against Jamming or Denial of Service to prevent unauthorized denial of legitimate engine start requests.

threats.threat_description: An attacker modifies the transmit control messages (DF14) from BCM to RF transceiver, injecting unauthorized challenges or changing transmission parameters to manipulate the RF communication.
threats.atm_technique_name: Reprogram Co-Located Computing Device for Privilege Escalation

cybersecurity_goal.csg_statement: The Body Control Module and RF Transceiver shall enforce the Authenticity, Integrity, and Availability of transmit control messages against Reprogram Co-Located Computing Device for Privilege Escalation to prevent unauthorized manipulation of RF-based vehicle entry and start systems.

threats.threat_description: Blocking or jamming the BCM to RF transceiver transmit control flow (DF14) prevents challenge messages from being sent, denying authentication.

cybersecurity_goal.csg_statement: The BCM to RF Transceiver Interface shall enforce the Availability and Authenticity of Remote Keyless Entry Communication against Jamming or Denial of Service to prevent denial of authorized vehicle access and operation.

threats.threat_description: An attacker manipulates or spoofs the analog RF waveform between RF transceiver and vehicle RF antenna (DF15), enabling relay or spoofing attacks that bypass proximity restrictions.

cybersecurity_goal.csg_statement: The RF Transceiver and Antenna subsystem shall enforce the Authenticity, Confidentiality, and Integrity of RF-based Proximity Authentication Data of RF_1 and ANT_RF_1 against ATM-T0007: Relay Communications to prevent unauthorized vehicle unlocking and starting.

threats.threat_description: Physical jamming or damage to the analog RF link (DF15) prevents transmission or reception of RF signals, denying authentication.

cybersecurity_goal.csg_statement: The RF Communication Module shall ensure the Availability and Authenticity of ANT_RF_1 against Jamming or Denial of Service to prevent loss of keyless entry and start functionality for legitimate users.

threats.threat_description: An attacker injects or manipulates the received RF waveform from the vehicle antenna to RF transceiver (DF16), enabling forged or replayed key fob responses.

cybersecurity_goal.csg_statement: The RF Transceiver (DF16) shall enforce the Authenticity, Integrity, and Availability of received RF communications on the ANT_RF_1 interface against ATM-T0003: Manipulate Communications to prevent unauthorized vehicle unlocking or starting.

threats.threat_description: Blocking or jamming the received RF waveform (DF16) prevents the RF transceiver from receiving key fob responses.

cybersecurity_goal.csg_statement: The RF Transceiver shall ensure the Availability of RF Signal Reception against Jamming or Denial of Service to prevent loss of remote keyless entry and vehicle starting functionality.

threats.threat_description: An attacker forges or injects false LF wake/proximity events in the internal flow from LF Receiver to BCM (DF17), causing unauthorized challenge triggering or denial of service.

cybersecurity_goal.csg_statement: The LF Receiver and BCM shall enforce the Authenticity and Availability of LF wake/proximity event communications against Manipulate Communications to prevent unauthorized keyless entry challenge triggering and denial of service.
cybersecurity_goal.verification_method: Test / Interface Fuzzing / Signal Injection Analysis

threats.threat_description: Blocking or jamming the LF Receiver to BCM event/control link (DF17) prevents legitimate wake signals from triggering challenge flow.

cybersecurity_goal.csg_statement: The LF Receiver to BCM communication link shall enforce the Availability and Authenticity of LF wake signals against Jamming or Denial of Service to prevent authorized users from being unable to unlock or start the vehicle.

threats.threat_description: An attacker modifies or forges HSM attestation or measurement reports sent to the BCM (DF18), undermining trust in the HSM integrity and enabling undetected compromise.

cybersecurity_goal.csg_statement: The Body Control Module (BCM) shall enforce the Authenticity and Integrity of attestation and measurement reports received from HSM_1 against Manipulate Communications to prevent acceptance of falsified HSM integrity proofs and undetected compromise.

threats.threat_description: Blocking or withholding HSM attestation/measurement data (DF18) from the BCM prevents integrity verification of the HSM, weakening system trust assurances.

cybersecurity_goal.csg_statement: The Body Control Module (BCM) shall enforce the Integrity, Availability, and Authenticity of HSM attestation and measurement data against Jamming or Denial of Service to prevent loss of trust in HSM integrity verification and unauthorized system operation.
